sub_chapter_briefs.title: Already in Motion
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: POV character is mid-action in a situation already under pressure — no warm-up, no setup. A specific, concrete problem is already happening. The reader is dropped in without orientation.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: POV character is mid-action in a situation already under pressure — no warm-up, no setup. A specific, concrete problem is already happening. The reader is dropped in without orientation.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Opening in medias res — drop into existing tension; no backstory, no scene-setting
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: TBD — to be specified when character roster and outline are populated
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Disoriented urgency; the reader feels the ground moving before they know where they are
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Establishes the chapter's central pressure and signals the book-level conflict is already in motion — no grace period for the protagonist

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The First Thing That Goes Wrong
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: The protagonist's first major obstacle lands — something that raises the stakes beyond the opening tension and forces a decision with real consequences. A point of no return is crossed.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: The protagonist's first major obstacle lands — something that raises the stakes beyond the opening tension and forces a decision with real consequences. A point of no return is crossed.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: First Crisis — initial escalation; forces an active decision; normal is no longer available
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Shock sharpening into resolve; the protagonist commits to a course of action they cannot walk back
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Locks the protagonist into the book's central conflict — the first crisis is the moment the larger story becomes unavoidable

sub_chapter_briefs.title: A Moment to Breathe (But Not to Rest)
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: A brief exhale after the first crisis. The protagonist has survived or adapted. One piece of backstory surfaces through action or dialogue. A detail is planted here that will matter at the climax. ESCALATION SEED: a small lie, hidden weakness, or misplaced trust is introduced here — small enough to seem inconsequential, large enough to detonate later.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: A brief exhale after the first crisis. The protagonist has survived or adapted. One piece of backstory surfaces through action or dialogue. A detail is planted here that will matter at the climax. ESCALATION SEED: a small lie, hidden weakness, or misplaced trust is introduced here — small enough to seem inconsequential, large enough to detonate later.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Mini-resolution after First Crisis — brief recovery; reveal backstory in motion; plant escalation seed
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Cautious relief undercut by unease; the reader senses the pause is borrowed time
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Deepens the protagonist's relationship to the book's central stakes; the planted detail or lie will reappear with greater pressure in a later chapter and explode at the book's turning point

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Worse Than the First
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: The second crisis hits harder and more personally than the first. Something the protagonist thought was settled is undone. A plan fails, a resource disappears, or a trust breaks. The protagonist is forced to confront something internal — not just external danger.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: The second crisis hits harder and more personally than the first. Something the protagonist thought was settled is undone. A plan fails, a resource disappears, or a trust breaks. The protagonist is forced to confront something internal — not just external danger.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Second Crisis — more personal, more costly; something breaks; protagonist confronts themselves
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Desperation edged with self-doubt; the emotional cost is now higher than the physical one
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Raises the book-level stakes by making the protagonist's internal flaw or fear visible — the book arc cannot resolve until this wound is addressed

sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Darkest Point
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: The third and most devastating crisis collapses everything the protagonist has been working toward. Their greatest fear is realized or their last resource is gone. The chapter ends not with resolution but with a new, urgent question that propels the reader into Chapter 3 — the chapter closes mid-motion.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: The third and most devastating crisis collapses everything the protagonist has been working toward. Their greatest fear is realized or their last resource is gone. The chapter ends not with resolution but with a new, urgent question that propels the reader into Chapter 3 — the chapter closes mid-motion.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Third Crisis into Climax — breaking point; everything collapses; chapter ends on an unresolved question that opens Chapter 3
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Bleak momentum; not despair but the cold clarity of someone who has run out of options and must act anyway
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: The chapter's third crisis is the book arc's first major escalation — what breaks here cannot be repaired without confronting the book's central conflict at full force
